title: LLM routing + KV prefetch - idea parking lot
content:
Context / goal:
- Reduce tail latency for chat-style workloads where repeated context hits (assistant memory, long-running sessions) matter.
- Reduce per-token cost by prefetching KV cache for likely next-turn prefixes and enabling smarter routing to cheaper model variants when appropriate.
- Keep behavior predictable for customers: explainability + safe fallbacks.

Problem statements (rough):
- Many customers see repeated prefixes across requests (session history, system prompts, personas) - we can pre-warm KV cache but need to avoid wasted work for low-likelihood prefixes.
- Routing decisions today are coarse: region/tier/model. We want request-level routing: latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive, and prefetched-KV-aware routing.
- Prefetch needs heuristics for which prefixes to precompute (N-grams? last-k-turns? intent classification?). Cache eviction and staleness also open questions.

Ideas / building blocks:
- Prefetch policy engine (local to serving node or central policy): given a request, predict top-k likely next prefixes to prefetch into KV cache. Lightweight predictor (LR or small transformer) trained on customer/session telemetry.
- Prefix scoring: score candidates by probability * benefit (latency reduction) * cost (compute). Tune threshold per-customer.
- Adaptive routing layer: if request has high probability prefetched KV for model A, route to dedicated pool optimized for that model; else route to lower-cost model variant with on-demand KV computation.
- Hybrid execution: start streaming tokens from cheaper model variant, and if a prefetched KV becomes available, switch to higher-quality model mid-request (needs token alignment / continuity). Risky but worth exploring for latency wins.
- Graceful fallback: if prefetch misses, fall back to non-prefetch model or queue for next-turn prefetch.

Rough PRD outline (very rough):
- Title: Request-aware routing + KV prefetch for chat workloads (alpha)
- Users: product teams building chat assistants, customer success for high-value customers, platform teams who want lower unit cost.
- Success metrics:  p95 latency reduction on chat workloads (target 20% for qualifying sessions), % of token generation served from prefetched KV, net cost delta (per-token cost reduction target 10% for baseline workloads), error/regression rate <= 1%.
- MVP scope:
  * Prefetch predictor running in serving runtime (configurable per-customer)
  * Routing policy that prefers nodes with prefetched KV when predictor confidence > threshold
  * Telemetry + dashboard: per-route hit-rate, prefetch cost, latency delta, missed-prefetch incidents
  * Manual opt-in per-customer + ability to pin models and disable prefetch
- Out-of-scope for MVP:
  * Hybrid mid-request model switching (exploratory)
notes:
Open questions / TODOs:
- Data for training predictor: use anonymized session traces? Need privacy review and opt-in.
- How to quantify cost of wasted prefetch vs latency benefit (real-time accounting).
- Interaction with caching across shards/nodes (consistency).
- Failure modes: prefetch causes degraded quality if KV mismatched - need validation.
- UI: allow customers to set policy (latency-first, cost-first, balanced).

Next steps / low-effort experiments:
- Run offline analysis on 2 weeks of chat traces: frequency of repeated prefixes, candidate k for prefetch, empirical probability distribution. (Zoe/analytics)
- Prototype predictor on small dataset (logistic regression over suffix grams + session features) and simulate prefetch hit-rate. (Raja)
- Add per-request routing flag in runtime that indicates "prefetch-hit-prob >= p" and route to dedicated test pool; measure. (Priya + infra)
- Draft Confluence PRD + quick design diagram for audit.

Links / references:
- Prior notes: users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json (local)
- Related: routing fallback notes, dynamic batching scraps

Random thoughts / heuristics (brain dump):
- Use entropy of next-token distribution as signal: low entropy -> safe to prefetch larger prefix?
- Short-term window: focus on last 2-3 turns for prefetch candidates; longer-term memory handled by dedicated memory service.
- For multimodal prompts or tool-calls, prefer no prefetch until we detect stable patterns.
- Rate-limit prefetch per-session to avoid DOS-style cost spikes.
